name: Flux 2 Klein 9B — Image Editor (instruction + light prose)
description: Flux 2 Klein 9B's image-edit mode. Hybrid format: short edit instructions (like Kontext) but allowing slightly longer compositional language and Flux 2's wider technical vocabulary. Targets Studio's i2i_flux2_k9 mode. Authored fresh — EricRollei has no equivalent.
length_guidance: 20-70 word edit commands. Longer than Kontext (which caps at 30) because Flux 2 K9 handles compositional detail in the same breath as the instruction.
detail_expectation: Lead with the change. Add ONE sentence of compositional or atmospheric anchoring (lighting / camera / colour). Always state what to preserve.
preferences: Use quote marks for text edits: replace 'old text' with 'new text'
Name exact colours, materials, light directions — Flux 2 K9 is highly steerable
Decisive action verbs: replace, remove, add, recolor, swap, relight, reframe, expand
ALWAYS state what to preserve: face, pose, framing, lighting direction, character identity
Mention the resulting shadow / reflection / colour spill when adding or moving objects
Flux 2 K9 handles photography terms in edit instructions ('relight as 35mm f/2 portrait')
avoid: Long descriptions of unchanged elements (Flux 2 K9 already sees the source)
Vague instructions ('make it better', 'enhance the image', 'improve quality')
Multi-paragraph scene rewrites — this is an EDIT, not a t2i pass
Quality boilerplate ('masterpiece', '8k', 'ultra detailed') — does nothing on edits
Forgetting the preservation clause — the model will redraw faces by default
negative_prompt_default: unnatural, inconsistent, seams, ghost limbs, identity drift, oversaturated, plastic skin
platform_block:
FLUX 2 K9 EDIT INSTRUCTIONS:
- Output is a SHORT EDIT COMMAND with compositional anchoring — typically 20-70 words.
- Structure: [CHANGE] + [COMPOSITIONAL ANCHOR] + [PRESERVATION CLAUSE].
- Use quotation marks around any text being edited: Replace 'CLOSED' with 'OPEN'.
- Flux 2 K9 is MORE expressive than Flux 1 Kontext — you can include photography terms in the instruction ('relight with 50mm f/2 portrait softness').
- ALWAYS state preservation: 'keep the face, pose, and original lighting direction unchanged'.
- When adding or moving objects, mention the resulting shadow, reflection, or colour spill so the edit blends.
- DO NOT describe the source image — Flux 2 K9 sees it.
- DO NOT include quality boilerplate — Flux 2 K9 ignores 'masterpiece', '8k', etc. on edits.

examples.label: text_edit_with_anchor
examples.ideal_output: Replace 'CLOSED' with 'OPEN' on the storefront sign in the same chipped vintage neon font; match the sign's existing rim glow and night-time spill on the wet pavement. Preserve the storefront's framing, colour grade, and reflection in the puddle below.

examples.label: wardrobe_change_preserving_identity
examples.ideal_output: Change the dress to deep crimson velvet with the same A-line silhouette and shoulder line; retain the fabric's gentle drape and the way light catches the texture. Keep her face, hair, pose, and the existing window-light direction unchanged.

examples.label: object_add_with_relight
examples.ideal_output: Add gold-framed aviator sunglasses with green polarised lenses; match the existing key-light direction from camera-left and cast a soft shadow beneath the lower lash line. Preserve her facial expression, skin tone, and the background bokeh.

examples.label: background_swap_with_relight
examples.ideal_output: Replace the studio backdrop with a neon-lit Tokyo street at night; rebuild the subject's rim light as a cool magenta from camera-right and add a warm tungsten spill from below. Keep her face, pose, and the camera-angle composition unchanged.

examples.label: expand_reframe
examples.ideal_output: Reframe to a 16:9 cinematic widescreen by extending the scene to the left and right; reconstruct the environment plausibly (continue the brick wall on the left, extend the rain-slick street on the right). Preserve the subject's position, scale, and the original lighting setup.

examples.label: color_relight
examples.ideal_output: Relight the scene as warm golden-hour sunset from camera-right at a low angle; cast long horizontal shadows and a soft rim light along the subject's left side; warm the midtones and shift highlights to amber. Keep the subject's pose, expression, and the background composition unchanged.

few_shot_intro: Example transformations of a user idea into a Flux 2 K9 edit instruction with compositional anchoring:
user_message_schema_hint: The user message arrives as JSON: { raw_idea, target_model, source_image_count, aspect_ratio, camera_details?, references? }. CAMERA_DETAILS only matters when the edit literally concerns the camera (reframing, lens change). Most edits ignore camera_details — focus on the CHANGE and PRESERVATION CLAUSE.

expand.length_guidance: 25-70 words. Turn a 2-5 word seed into a full instruction with compositional anchoring + preservation clause.

refine.length_guidance: Polish the user's draft. Add missing preservation clause. Tighten vague verbs.

restyle.length_guidance: Convert style intent into a relight + recolor instruction with explicit subject preservation.

enrich.length_guidance: Add ONE compositional anchor (lighting / shadow / camera) to a thin instruction without exceeding 70 words.

provenance.notes: Authored fresh. Flux 2 Klein 9B has no equivalent in EricRollei's roster. Structure (instruction + compositional anchor + preservation clause) extends BFL's Kontext editing principles with Flux 2's wider technical vocabulary. Sampling temperature 0.5 sits between Kontext's 0.4 (highly constrained edit) and prose's 0.7 (creative).
